name: Fields of the Wood
unique: A hillside park where the Ten Commandments are laid out in letters large enough to walk on, along with a giant hand, a tomb, a baptismal pool and a path of biblical scenes climbing Burger Mountain.
buzz: People come for the scale of the lettering and stay for the walk up. Believers treat it as devotion and non believers treat it as one of the strangest and most sincere roadside spectacles in the mountains.

name: Hiwassee Lake
dates: Year round, best spring to fall
unique: Six thousand acres of deep mountain water in a flooded river valley with more than a hundred miles of shoreline, ringed by national forest, stocked with walleye and striped bass and quiet enough to have coves to yourself on a weekday.
buzz: Anglers chase the walleye and the striped bass and say the lake fishes best at night in summer. The mountains come right down to the water and there is almost no development on the national forest side.

name: Snowbird Creek
company: U.S. Forest Service, Nantahala National Forest
unique: A creek in the Snowbird Mountains with a trail that climbs past waterfalls and old logging railroad grades into the Joyce Kilmer Slickrock Wilderness, where the forest is old growth and the water is cold enough for native brook trout.
buzz: Wild trout anglers keep it quiet and hikers do the falls and turn around. The upper trail is steep, faint in places and one of the wilder walks in the state.

name: Murphy Courthouse Square
unique: A square in the westernmost county seat in North Carolina, with an 1890s courthouse, a monument and storefronts a few blocks from the Hiwassee River and the Tennessee line.
buzz: Small and quiet, with the river close and the mountains on three sides. People stop on the way to the lake or the forest trails.

name: Mount Jefferson State Natural Area
dates: Year round; summit road closed in winter ice
unique: A mountain that rises more than sixteen hundred feet above the surrounding valley to a summit over five thousand feet, with a short summit trail, cliffs of rock that glow at sunset and plant communities found nowhere else in the state.
buzz: The drive up is steep and the summit trail is short, which makes it the best effort to reward ratio in the high country. Sunset from the top is the local recommendation.

name: Ashe County Cheese
cost: Free to watch, cheese priced per item
unique: The oldest cheese factory in the South, on Main Street in West Jefferson, with a viewing room where you watch curds being cut and cheddared through a window, and a shop selling cheese made on site.
buzz: The viewing room is free and children like the machinery. People come for the cheese curds and the hoop cheese and leave with more than they planned.

name: New River State Park
cost: Free, canoe access and camping small fee
unique: A state park strung along the New River, one of the oldest rivers in North America, with canoe access points, primitive campsites on the banks and a current gentle enough for families with children.
buzz: Paddlers do the two day float and camp on the river, and anglers fish the pools for smallmouth. The river is slow and shallow and the mountains close in on both sides.

name: Cumberland Knob
dates: April to November, parkway weather dependent
company: National Park Service, Blue Ridge Parkway
unique: The spot where the first section of the Blue Ridge Parkway was built by Depression era crews in the 1930s, with a short trail around the knob, a picnic area and a stone comfort station from the same era.
buzz: It is the least crowded and most historically interesting stop on the parkway's North Carolina end. The trail is easy and the view south into the valley is the reward.

name: Doughton Park
company: National Park Service, Blue Ridge Parkway
unique: Seven thousand acres of parkway high country with more than thirty miles of trail, including the walk to Brinegar Cabin, a preserved mountain farmstead, and open balds where the views run into Virginia.
buzz: Hikers rate the Bluff Mountain and Flat Rock loops among the best on the parkway and the crowds stay at the overlooks. Spring wildflowers and October color are the seasons.

name: Sparta Downtown
unique: A small mountain town with a courthouse, a main street of shops and a bluegrass and old time music tradition that fills the auditorium on Saturday nights.
buzz: The music is the reason people come and the town is small enough that the pickers know each other. Visitors describe being pulled into a jam before they finish their coffee.

name: Emerald Hollow Mine
unique: The only emerald mine in the United States open to the public, where you pay for a permit, take a shovel and a bucket to the creek or the digging area and keep whatever you find, from quartz and mica to the green beryl the county is named for.
buzz: Families with children do the sluice and the creek and go home with a bucket of rocks. Serious rockhounds dig the hard rock and find emeralds and hiddenite, and the staff will identify what you found.

name: Taylorsville Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse and a ring of shops in a county that was furniture and textiles before it was gemstones, between the Brushy Mountains and the Catawba valley.
buzz: Small and plain, and the place to eat before or after the mine. People who come for emeralds are surprised the town is this quiet.

name: Ramsour's Mill Battleground
company: Lincoln County and local historical groups
unique: The hillside where on June 20, 1780, Patriot and Loyalist militia from the same North Carolina counties fought each other in one of the largest all North Carolina actions of the Revolution, with markers, a monument and the slope still open.
buzz: It is a quiet hillside with a stone monument and almost nobody there. People who find it are usually reading their way through the southern campaign and say the ground explains the fight.

name: Lincolnton Courthouse Square
unique: A square with an 1920s courthouse, brick storefronts and a monument, in a town that was a Revolutionary War crossroads and later a cotton and furniture mill center on the South Fork.
buzz: The square is well kept and the antique shops are the draw. It is a twenty minute walk and a good lunch stop off the highway.

name: Lincoln County Museum of History
unique: A county collection of documents, photographs, textiles and household goods from a county that fought a battle, built cotton mills and made Furniture, in a small building on the edge of downtown.
buzz: Volunteers run it and the family files are the reason genealogists visit. Small and free and glad of the company.

name: Cooleemee Mill Town
unique: A textile mill village laid out by Erwin Mills at the end of the nineteenth century, with rows of identical mill houses, a company store building and a museum of the mill and the people who worked it.
buzz: The mill is gone and the village is not, and the historical association has kept the story. People who grew up in mill towns come back to walk the streets.

name: Mocksville Downtown
unique: A main street with a 1900s courthouse, a brick commercial block and a restaurant or two, in a piedmont county that has stayed agricultural while the cities around it grew.
buzz: Quiet and easy, and the downtown has been steadily restored. People stop off I-40 for lunch and find the square emptier than they expected.

name: Yadkin County Wine Trail
unique: A cluster of more than a dozen family wineries around Yadkinville, East Bend, Jonesville and Hamptonville, growing vinifera and muscadine on the piedmont slopes of the Yadkin Valley, North Carolina's first American Viticultural Area.
buzz: The tasting rooms are small and the pourers are often the owners. People do three or four in a day and stop for lunch in Yadkinville.

name: Yadkinville Courthouse Square
unique: A small square with a 1900s courthouse and a few storefronts, in a county named for the river that made the valley good for grapes.
buzz: Two blocks and a couple of shops. It is the place to get a sandwich between tasting rooms.

name: Yadkin River
unique: A piedmont river running through the county with rocky shoals, wooded banks and public accesses, shallow enough to wade and slow enough to float when the water is up.
buzz: Local anglers fish the pools for bass and paddlers run it after rain. It is a working river with no facilities, so bring two cars.
